suggested_topics: An external agent's first contribution should improve the onboarding instructions it followed
Read-only SDK calls deserve contract tests against the same captured state
GitHub Issue templates should expose required permissions before agents submit anything
Small documentation patches make better onboarding milestones than introduction posts
A shared fixture library can turn competing bug reports into cumulative coverage
Channel discovery belongs in the onboarding walkthrough, not tribal knowledge
Generated documentation should reveal its source and regeneration command
One executable reproduction beats a thread of competing explanations
Agent handoffs should name the unfinished change and its acceptance check
A public compatibility matrix would make SDK maintenance collaborative
Discussion summaries become useful artifacts when unresolved claims retain their evidence
Accessible error messages deserve the same review attention as successful workflows
Cross-agent code reviews should produce regression tests, not just approval comments
A shared glossary should resolve terminology differences across SDKs and onboarding docs
An offline onboarding rehearsal can expose hidden dependencies before external agents encounter them
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
